summary: Statistics Finland publishes, every year, child victims of sexual, violent and abuse-material offences by origin (Finnish or foreign background) and suspects by origin and background-country region with rates per 10,000. Origin is based on parents' country of birth, a proxy, never ethnicity.

european_title: Not recorded by any Finnish source
european_note: Finnish statistics record origin and background country from parents' country of birth, never ethnicity. Finnish background plus foreign background from the four European regions is the closest any country in this batch comes to 'European background', and it is shown as a calculated group. It is still a proxy: Finnish background includes grandchildren of immigrants and anyone with one Finnish-born parent, and the regions are birth-country geography, not descent.
proxy_note: Finland records origin and background country (parents' country of birth), never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Rape of a child (police statistics)
harms.intro: Police recorded 551 child victims (0-17) of rape or aggravated rape of a child and 1,877 of sexual assault or abuse of a child in 2025, and 585 and 762 suspects of the same offences. Statistics Finland publishes victims by origin and suspects by origin and background-country region, with suspect rates per 10,000, every year.

victims.scope: Finland, child victims (0-17) of rape or aggravated rape of a child recorded by the police, 2025
victims.rate_reason: Statistics Finland publishes no victim rates by origin; for context, foreign-background children were 15.1% of children aged 0-14 at the end of 2025 (calculated here from table 11rt).
victims.share_note: StatFin table 141k (victims by offence heading, 2025). Counts: Finnish background 482 (born in Finland 471, abroad 11), foreign background 67 (born abroad 37, in Finland 30), unknown 2; shares calculated here. Origin (Statistics Finland): 'Finnish background' means at least one parent was born in Finland, so it includes grandchildren of immigrants and children with one foreign-born parent; 'foreign background' means both parents (or the only known parent) were born abroad, split into those born abroad (first generation) and born in Finland (second generation). Background country is the parents' country of birth (the mother's first). This is a birth-country proxy, not ethnicity.

breakdown.why: Statistics Finland publishes 2025 child victims (0-17) of rape and sexual abuse of a child by origin (Finnish or foreign background, born in Finland or abroad) and suspects of the same offences by origin and background-country region with rates per 10,000. Origin is based on parents' birth country, a proxy; victims and suspects not linked. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Child assault victims (11,304 in 2025) and child victims of domestic violence by a parent (2,761) by origin; assault suspects by origin and background region with rates, all victims. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Child victims of offences against life (5 in 2025, all Finnish background) and of attempts (26) by origin; suspects of offences against life (74) by origin and background region, all victims. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Police statistics give 16 child trafficking victims in 2025 by origin; the National Assistance System gives its 271 new clients by nationality (18 Finns, 10 minors). No trafficker origin. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Child victims of child sexual abuse material offences (187 in 2025) by origin; suspects of online child sexual offences and online abuse-material offences by origin and background region with rates. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: Finland scores 15% on the stricter scale (0-20%), the best data in this batch. Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. Statistics Finland publishes, every year, child victims of sexual, violent and abuse-material offences by origin and suspects by origin and background-country region with rates, so Finnish-background and European-background groups can be told apart from others. Origin is still based on parents' birth country, a proxy. The 25% cap is not what sets this score, because heritage points are already 0.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
